title: Paramartha Guru Tale 44

full_text:
A wealthy patron presented Guru Paramartha with a small cloth bag containing five hundred tiny, golden mustard seeds of an exceptionally rare, aromatic Himalayan variety, used for temple offerings.

While Matti was carrying the bag to the altar, the bottom seam unravelled, and thirty tiny mustard seeds spilled onto the mud floor of the ashram veranda, scattering among the dust.

Matti was in despair: 'Master! Thirty sacred mustard seeds have fallen into the dust! If we sweep them with a broom, they will be crushed; if we leave them, the ashram mice will eat them!'

The Guru stroked his beard: 'Every seed is sacred! Recover all thirty seeds without losing one!'

The disciples knelt on the floor, attempting to pick up the tiny seeds with their fingers. But their fingers were large and clumsy, and the tiny seeds slipped into the fine cracks between the floorboards.

Madayan devised an extraordinary biological retrieval plan: 'The Ant Labor Cooperative!'

'Explain your plan, Madayan,' said the Guru.

Madayan expounded: 'Ants are professional gatherers of seeds! Their mandibles are microscopically precise! If we invite a colony of red ants onto the floor, they will gather all thirty mustard seeds and carry them to their anthill! Then we can simply dig up the anthill and collect our seeds!'

Matti ran to the garden, broke off a branch from a mango tree covered with thousands of vicious, stinging red tree-ants, and shook the branch over the veranda floor!

Thousands of furious, stinging red ants rained down upon the floorboards!

Instead of gathering the mustard seeds, the enraged ants swarmed over the bare feet, ankles, and legs of Guru Paramartha and his disciples!

Within seconds, hundreds of fiery, agonizing stings bit into the holy men's flesh!

The Guru shrieked, hopping like a madman: 'AI-YO! THE WORKERS ARE ON STRIKE! THEY ARE EATING MY ANKLES!'

The disciples danced around the veranda, slapping their legs and howling in pain: 'FIRE! FIRE ON OUR LEGS!'

Running to the garden well, they poured buckets of cold water over their legs to wash away the stinging ants.

Sitting on the grass, covered in painful, burning red welts, Guru Paramartha looked at his swollen feet.

The thirty tiny mustard seeds remained peacefully in the cracks of the floorboards, completely ignored.

The Guru sighed with profound resignation: 'The ant labor force was uncooperative; let the floorboards keep the mustard seeds as rent!'
moral: Fretting over microscopic losses wastes the hours needed to secure the harvest.
